title: Toolchain Contracts and Safe Execute Demo with Celadon Works
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console + API showing JSON-mode contracts, tool/function invocation patterns, runtime fallbacks and guardrails. Customer focused on safe execution, VPC/KMS, and predictable latency for user-facing flows.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share security whitepaper + SOC2 report by 2026-03-09
Ethan Patel: Run a 5k inference latency benchmark on Celadon's sample traffic and share results by 2026-03-12
Rajiv Kumar: Provide 1 week of anonymized sample traffic for routing/cost modeling by 2026-03-11
next_steps: Set up pilot environment (dedicated pool with VPC) - target start week of 2026-03-22
Redwood to produce cost/latency estimate sheet after receiving sample traffic
Security deep-dive scheduled with Ben on 2026-03-10 10:00 PT
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-07 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
transcript: 00:00:04 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:00:08 Rajiv Kumar: Rajiv here, CTO at Celadon Works.
00:00:11 Tara Miles: Tara, lead ML eng.
00:00:13 Ben Torres: Ben, security.
00:00:16 Samir Nair: Samir, platform.

00:00:20 Maya Chen: Awesome. I'm Maya, AE for Redwood. Ethan (SE) will run through the console and show the JSON-mode execute patterns and guardrails. We'll roughly go 30 minutes demo and then q and a, sound good?

00:00:33 Ethan Patel: Hi all. quick note: I'll be switching between console and the API to show contract enforcement, tool calling, and runtime fallbacks. Some of the names in the transcript might get munged by auto-AT, apologies in advance.
00:00:46 Tara Miles: sounds good, we're especially curious about how you guarantee no exfil with tool calls and how the fallback policies behave under load.
00:00:55 Ethan Patel: great, we'll cover KMS integration, VPC private endpoints, and the audit trail as part of that.

00:01:10 Ethan Patel: opening the console - first pane is the model catalog, you can pin variants and see verified perf. I'm going to pick a 40B quantized variant for demo purposes, note you can choose hosted or dedicated runtime here.
00:01:28 Ben Torres: is that quantization preserving top-k sampling determinism? we've seen hallucination spikes before with some quantized runtimes.

00:01:36 Ethan Patel: short answer: we include a quant profile with recommendation for sampling temps and top-p; it reduces divergence in many cases. also we've got monitoring for quality drift tied to your eval sets.
00:01:52 Tara Miles: can we enforce a json schema for outputs so our downstream tool doesn't break?

00:01:57 Ethan Patel: yes - switching to JSON mode. here we upload a contract schema; we call it an action contract. the engine will attempt to produce structured JSON matching the schema, and if it doesn't, the runtime applies a repair path or runtime fallback.
00:02:15 Ethan Patel: showing the schema file now - fields: user_intent, entities:list, confidence:float, actions:list(actionType, params).
00:02:28 Rajiv Kumar: hold on, what happens if the model returns unstructured text or tries to call an external tool it shouldn't?

00:02:33 Ethan Patel: good question. two things: at the sandbox level, tool/function calling requires a registered action in the console. if the model suggests a function not registered, the runtime will either map to a safe fallback or return a structured error object depending on the contract policy.
00:02:51 Ethan Patel: also the console's safety gating allows you to whitelist allowed external endpoints and tie each to network ACLs in the VPC mode.
00:03:03 Ben Torres: and encryption at rest for the KV cache and logs?
00:03:06 Ethan Patel: yes KMS for keys; we support customer-managed KMS keys for Private and Dedicated. logs are optionally sent to your SIEM via secure egress in VPC mode.
00:03:18 Tara Miles: show us the API payload for a call that triggers a tool—we want to see the shape.

00:03:22 Ethan Patel: switching to API tab. example request: model:redwood-40q, mode:json, contract_id:celadon_invoice_action, input:{text:...}, tools:[payment-lookup, customer-db-read]. here the tools array lists allowed invocations with IDs.
00:03:45 Tara Miles: ok and the response shows the actions array when the model chooses to call a tool?

00:03:49 Ethan Patel: exact. here's a demo response - you'll see actions:[{"actionType":"customer_lookup","params":{"customer_id":"123"}}], then the runtime performs the registered call to the tool connector.
00:04:04 Rajiv Kumar: how do you prevent data exfil through tool params? e.g., model returning a secret as param?

00:04:10 Ethan Patel: we have parameter-level sanitizers and allow-listing for data types. plus runtime will redact secret-like patterns before forwarding to connectors. for extra safety you can enforce a transform function that validates param schema against a whitelist.
00:04:26 Ben Torres: is that transform code customer-owned? where does it run?
00:04:30 Ethan Patel: it can be customer-supplied and executed in your private VPC for Private deployments; for hosted we run the transform in an isolated sandbox and provide attestations.
00:04:42 Samir Nair: latency-wise, if you do a tool call mid-generation, what's the expected impact? we're very latency-sensitive for UI paths.

00:04:47 Ethan Patel: good call. we support synchronous and asynchronous tool calls. for latency-sensitive paths we recommend prefetching and using the runtime's KV cache to avoid round trips; or use a canary tool that responds quickly. in dedicated mode you can pin capacity to keep single-digit hundred ms tail latencies.
00:05:05 Tara Miles: earlier you mentioned repair paths if the model misses schema. show that flow.

00:05:09 Ethan Patel: yes - if response fails validation, the runtime applies a repair step: it invokes the same model with a constrained prompt asking to only correct the invalid fields, or it falls back to a deterministic parser that extracts entities. policies are configurable per-contract.
00:05:25 Rajiv Kumar: can we get metrics on how often repairs happen? we want to track quality regressions over time.
00:05:29 Ethan Patel: absolutely; console includes per-contract telemetry: validity rate, repair rate, avg correction tokens, and a diff view showing before/after with examples.
00:05:40 Maya Chen: quick qualification—timeline? what's your target for a pilot and where would an eval sit in your procurement?
00:05:47 Rajiv Kumar: ideally pilot this quarter, procurement sign-off by end of month if security checks look clean.
00:05:55 Maya Chen: perfect. we'll prioritize the security pack. Ethan, can you demo an actual end-to-end call with a registered tool and a fallback?
00:06:01 Ethan Patel: yes. I'm going to simulate a user utterance: 'Find latest invoice for customer 123 and check payment status', sending to the JSON contract.
00:06:12 [00:06:12] API Request Sent
00:06:16 [00:06:16] Model Response (raw): 'Sure, pulling up customer info...customer id is one two three. Looks like last invoice 2026-02-28 paid via last four 4321, but this might be sensitive'

00:06:31 Ethan Patel: that raw output would violate parameter rules. runtime detects pattern 'last four' and redacts to ANON. Then it returns an actions array with customer_lookup and invoice_status_check.
00:06:45 Tara Miles: that redaction step is automatic? can we tune the regex?
00:06:49 Ethan Patel: yes it's configurable. you can provide regex patterns or use the built-in heuristics. for Private deployments, you can also bring your own sanitizer module.
00:07:02 Rajiv Kumar: show the audit record please.
00:07:05 Ethan Patel: opening the audit trail—each request has event IDs, chain of tool invocations, pre- and post-sanitized params, and optionally a signed attestation if using customer KMS.
00:07:18 Ben Torres: does attestation include a hash of the transform code and KMS key ID?
00:07:22 Ethan Patel: yes. it includes key ID, code hash, and TIMESTAMP. you can export the audit log to your SIEM or S3 with encryption.
00:07:35 Samir Nair: let's talk routing/fallbacks - if dedicated pool saturates, do you degrade to hosted older model variants?

00:07:41 Ethan Patel: exactly. smart routing rules let you fail over to a cheaper/compatible model or to a lower latency region. you can set cost or latency thresholds to trigger routing policies; we also keep per-customer quotas to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
00:07:55 Tara Miles: and how do you validate compatibility between model variants and action contracts?

00:08:00 Ethan Patel: during model onboarding we run a contract compatibility check which runs a sample corpus and measures schema conformity; weights are assigned and incompatible models are flagged for downgrade.
00:08:12 Rajiv Kumar: what about offline inference for air-gapped infra? we've got some regulated clients asking for on-prem options.
00:08:18 Ethan Patel: Redwood Private supports on-prem packages. runtime and orchestration control plane can be deployed behind your firewall. you'll manage KMS and connectors locally.
00:08:29 Ben Torres: show me the security page for connectors - I'd like to see least privilege config.

00:08:33 Ethan Patel: opening connector config - each connector has a role and scope; for example customer-db-read only allows SELECT on specific tables via service account. connectors run in your VPC when Private is used.
00:08:50 Tara Miles: one more: can we run smoke tests that simulate bad inputs to exercise guardrails?
00:08:54 Ethan Patel: yes, console has a 'fuzz test' runner for contracts. it will run thousands of permutations against your contract and report violation types. we'll include that in the pilot.
00:09:07 Rajiv Kumar: can you map cost back to tokens per route? we need to forecast costs for peak TPS.

00:09:12 Ethan Patel: Console Optimize provides token-level cost breakdowns by route, model variant, and caching hit rate. with sample traffic we can model monthly costs under different batching and caching configs.
00:09:26 Maya Chen: pause for quick Qs from Celadon security? Ben?
00:09:30 Ben Torres: yes, on multi-tenancy: are logs and caches isolated per customer in dedicated?
00:09:34 Ethan Patel: yes dedicated pools have per-tenant isolation; KV cache is namespaced per-customer and can be physically isolated on Dedicated.
00:09:46 Ben Torres: do you rotate KMS keys automatically?
00:09:49 Ethan Patel: you can enable automatic rotation or manage it yourself for customer-managed keys.
00:09:56 Tara Miles: can we run a quick demo of a failing contract and show the repair?

00:09:59 Ethan Patel: sure. I'm going to send a deliberately malformed response now, model returns plain text instead of JSON. runtime notices validation failure, triggers repair pass with a constrained prompt. show response: repaired JSON with corrected fields plus metadata: repair_reason: 'missing fields', repair_tokens: 18.
00:10:25 Rajiv Kumar: nice. can we get a webhook when repair rate exceeds X%?
00:10:29 Ethan Patel: yes, you can configure alerts - repair rate, validity drop, or cost per route. alerts can go to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook.
00:10:40 Maya Chen: quick sales note: pilot pricing usually includes a small usage bucket and a flat onboarding fee for dedicated setup. I'll follow up with specifics.
00:10:48 Rajiv Kumar: procurement will need the customer agreement and SOC2 asap.
00:10:52 Maya Chen: we'll send the agreements and SOC2 link right after. Ethan, back to the technicals — any caveats?

00:10:58 Ethan Patel: main caveats: schema design matters — overly permissive unions can hide errors; pre-warming dedicated pools helps tail latencies; and for extremely sensitive PII flows bring transforms on-prem.
00:11:14 Tara Miles: what about developer ergonomics, how easy to onboard engineers to build and test contracts?
00:11:19 Ethan Patel: Console has contract templates, unit test harness, and local CLI that mirrors runtime validation. also an SDK with typed bindings in Python and TypeScript.
00:11:32 Samir Nair: can we integrate the SDK into our CI to gate merges if contract regressions appear?
00:11:36 Ethan Patel: yes, the CLI can run contract checks in CI, failing builds on schema drift beyond thresholds.
00:11:45 Ben Torres: show me an example audit export for a single request - we want to see the event chain.

00:11:50 Ethan Patel: exporting now - sample CSV/JSON includes request_id, contract_id, actions_invoked, pre_sanitized_params, post_sanitized_params, attestation_hash. note pre_sanitized is masked by default but retained for internal debugging if you permit it.
00:12:07 Rajiv Kumar: are there SLA numbers for dedicated? our SLAs require 99.9 for 95th percentile latency on inference.
00:12:13 Ethan Patel: dedicated plans include configurable SLOs with financial credit tiers; we can commit 99.9 on a contract with pinned capacity and observability hooks.
00:12:24 Tara Miles: what's the onboarding timeline for dedicated with VPC and KMS?
00:12:28 Maya Chen: typically 2-4 weeks depending on connector complexity; we'll fast-track if procurement clears the initial paperwork.
00:12:36 Rajiv Kumar: ok good. how do rollbacks work if we push a contract update and it breaks things?

00:12:41 Ethan Patel: console supports versioned contracts with canary rollout. you can route N% of traffic, monitor repair/validity metrics, then promote or rollback automatically based on thresholds.
00:12:54 Tara Miles: show me the canary UI - how granular is the routing?
00:12:57 Ethan Patel: routing by route, by region, or by customer_id hashing. we also have time-of-day and cost-based rules.
00:13:07 Ben Torres: any examples of customers who used the repair pipeline to catch regressions?
00:13:11 Ethan Patel: yeah, one fintech client reduced manual support tickets by 40% by enforcing contracts + automatic repairs and alerting when repairs spiked.
00:13:23 Rajiv Kumar: regarding cost forecasting, can you show us the Optimize recommendations?

00:13:27 Ethan Patel: sure. Optimize shows a suggested quantization profile, batch sizes for your traffic shape, cache TTL recommendations, and projected savings. it's a weighted model: quality delta vs cost delta.
00:13:40 Tara Miles: will you include model A/B test support so we can test two variants for quality vs cost?
00:13:44 Ethan Patel: yes, console supports A/B for contracts: route 50/50 and gather contract validity, repair rates and downstream success metrics.
00:13:56 Samir Nair: final question from me: how do you handle schema migrations - if downstream changes contract shape?

00:14:02 Ethan Patel: we recommend semver on contracts. console can validate additive vs breaking changes and will reject non-backwards compatible updates unless flagged. we also support transformation adapters so old consumers can still read new payloads.
00:14:16 Tara Miles: that's handy. ok, ready for Q&A from Ben?
00:14:20 Ben Torres: yes, regarding penetration testing: do you allow RED-team style tests?
00:14:24 Ethan Patel: we do for enterprise customers under NDA; we can arrange a coordinated pentest window and share a test plan.
00:14:33 Rajiv Kumar: are there any known limitations to watch for? like very long context windows with large KV caches?
00:14:38 Ethan Patel: performance depends on sequence length and cache hit rate; extremely long histories can increase latency. we recommend summarization strategies and intelligent prefix caching.
00:14:50 Maya Chen: great — wrapping up: we're committed to getting security docs today, a bench plan from Ethan, and Rajiv will provide sample traffic. any final asks?
00:14:59 Rajiv Kumar: just the SOC2 and the sample traffic. Also please include a quick guide for CI contract checks.
00:15:07 Maya Chen: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff and security deep dive.
00:15:15 Tara Miles: thanks, this was helpful.
00:15:18 Ben Torres: thanks all.
00:15:20 Ethan Patel: thanks, signing off soon - I'll attach a short runbook and the sample API calls.
00:15:24 [Meeting end transcript cut here — recording continued with noise for a few seconds]
00:16:00 Final Notes: Demo lasted ~40 minutes with 8 minutes of Q&A; recording saved to shared drive and security packet to be sent via secure link.
